mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active and driven by the level of FEDFUNDS relative to its recent trend.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior month but 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0% for the current month, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for the current month, the 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal a broad-based weakening of consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings growth expectations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline by at least 1.0% month-over-month, the 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below its 3-month moving average), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced manufacturing output and corporate profit expectations.
failure_condition: In periods when INDPRO is below its 3-month moving average, the 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.0% indicates a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases corporate borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%, the 5-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent quarterly declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a prolonged weakening of consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline by at least 2.0% over the past quarter, the 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of rising industrial production (INDPRO above its 3-month moving average), the S&P 500 experiences positive returns over the next 20 trading days due to expanding manufacturing output and stronger corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: In periods when INDPRO is above its 3-month moving average, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past month signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS declines by at least 0.5% over the prior month, the 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances.
